page: Microsoft Azure E4as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EASv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, though it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data reveals a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% on stress-ng tests, and Geekbench single-core scores are average. However, multi-core performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25% for both stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth is also relatively low, with uncached read and write speeds categorized in the bottom 25%. This indicates that while individual threads execute efficiently, highly parallelized workloads and memory-intensive data transfers may face performance bottlenecks.

Given its hardware profile, the E4as_v5 is qualitatively cost-effective for workloads requiring a larger memory footprint without demanding high multi-core compute density. It is suitable for memory-intensive applications such as medium-sized databases, caching layers, and lightweight enterprise applications. It is less suited for high-throughput web serving, parallel software compilation, or intensive LLM inference, where its multi-threaded and memory bandwidth limitations are more pronounced.
